newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa falls sharply, ending week-long rally.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa falls sharply, ending week-long rally.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures took a tumble in a late sell-off on Wednesday and tentatively ended a week-long rally that had hoisted prices to one-year highs, traders said.
Trade selling emerged in late afternoon to knock prices to the lowest level since June 23. The setback also followed a sharp technical correction to an overbought market.
The pace was also intensified by tumbling New York cocoa futures as the market breached key chart support at $1,655.
LIFFE's September gapped 11 stg down at the open and ended the day a steep 50 stg down at 1,108 a tonne, but just above a major support at 1,100. Other traded months also posted heavy losses.
Just a day earlier, the September position finished at a contract high of 1,160 although it failed to match the June 1996 peak of 1,172 based on the second-month.
Traders said the uptrend, which has seen prices rising by 14 percent in three weeks, could remain intact if September holds the 1,100 support.
Others said the losses in New York and London were not unexpected as the recent rapid rise had led the market into a vacuum.
The day's volume totalled 3,231 lots after standing at just 477 at midday.
Cocoa's rally since mid-June was fuelled by aggressive fund-led and industry buying amid improved chart picture and the longer-term adverse impact of the El Nino weather pattern on future harvests.

In other news, mid-crop cocoa arrivals from Ivory Coast looked set to increase from late July. Arrivals totalled 50,000 tonnes from end-June but still had the potential to reach 150,000 by end-August.
Europe's second-quarter cocoa grind figures, due this week or early next, were expected to show mixed trends.
But traders doubt if the data will have any impact on the market. --Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
